progress.text: Gradient panel presets: a Presets menu applies one of the built-in gradient libraries' presets (grouped by theme) or a saved one to the gradient behind the active proxy, keeping its placement, as one undo step; the panel menu saves the current gradient as a preset, kept with the preferences, and deletes saved ones (gradient.presets.list/apply/save/delete).

Linux: the Flatpak on GNOME copies and pastes text with other apps through the compositor's core Wayland protocol (smithay-clipboard on the window's connection), where arboard has neither data-control nor X11. Scores and estimates unchanged.

Linux: a clipboard that can't be opened (the Flatpak on GNOME, where arboard has neither data-control nor X11) is retried after 1 s, doubling to a minute, and logged once, where the background Paste check used to reconnect and log a warning every 250 ms (267k warnings in 18 h). Scores and estimates unchanged.

Pathfinder › Trap: the Pathfinder panel's Trap… and Effect › Pathfinder › Trap… add a thin overprinting strip of the lighter colour inside the darker one where two solid colours meet, so misregistered plates leave no gap (trapping), with Thickness, Height/Width, Tint Reduction, Traps with Process Color and Reverse Traps. Illustrator effects 49/50 (SVG Filters remains); Live vector effects hours 6–10 → 4–8; headline numbers unchanged.

OpenType SVG colour fonts draw as vector art: each glyph's SVG document is read by the SVG importer, in the text's colours where it asks for them, and draws, exports and outlines as COLR glyphs do; all colour font formats are now drawn.

COLR colour fonts (v0 and v1, as in Noto Color Emoji's vector build, Segoe UI Emoji, Nabla) draw as vector art: their layers' colours, gradients, clips and blend modes on the canvas and in SVG, EPS, legacy .ai and PDF, and as editable paths with Create Outlines; glyphs using sweep gradients or compositing modes are drawn as images of the glyph.

The Effect Gallery shipped (#2883): Effect › Effect Gallery… browses the Artistic, Brush Strokes, Distort, Sketch, Stylize and Texture filters, edits each filter's settings, builds an ordered stack (add, reorder, hide, remove) with a live canvas preview, and OK applies it as separate appearance effects in one undo step. Filter thumbnails and a preview area inside the dialog remain (Filter Gallery overview). Raster effects 82% → 85% (estimated); headline numbers unchanged.

Colour emoji fonts with bitmap glyphs draw and export: sbix (Apple Color Emoji, macOS's emoji font) and CBDT (bitmap Noto Color Emoji) glyphs show as their pictures on the canvas, whatever the type's fill, scale and turn with the type, and export to PDF (in the font's Type 3 glyphs, or as images), SVG (images when type is outlined; live text leaves emoji to the viewer), EPS and legacy .ai (images); Create Outlines turns them into embedded images. Fonts with bitmaps but no outlines, such as Noto Color Emoji, are now found among the installed fonts. COLR and OpenType SVG fonts remain; headline numbers unchanged.

Effect › Sketch › Conté Crayon: a black crayon in the dark areas and a white one in the light areas, on mid-grey paper whose texture (Brick, Burlap, Canvas, Sandstone; Scaling, Relief, Light Direction, Invert) breaks the strokes, with Foreground Level and Background Level; an original approximation, defaults unverified. Every Photoshop-style filter is now in (57/57); the Effect Gallery remains (4–6 h).

Ruby (ふりがな) for live text: type.ruby sets or removes a reading over a byte range of the selected type — above it in horizontal type, right of the column in vertical type (or below/left), start/centre/end aligned, at 1–100% of the base size (default half), overhanging or squeezed to the base width. It is saved in the native file, laid out with its line growing (following lines move on), drawn on the canvas, and written in SVG and PDF as outlines where ruby is present. UI panel and type on a path are next. Headline numbers unchanged.

PDF accessibility: titled exports set /ViewerPreferences << /DisplayDocTitle true >>, so viewers show the document title rather than the file name and title checks can pass (#3646). Headline numbers unchanged.
3D lighting: four original lighting presets shared by Revolve, Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate, with command access and manual Custom settings; scores and estimates unchanged.

Print: the Print dialog's Media list has the Japanese papers — JIS B4 (257 × 364 mm), JIS B5 (182 × 257 mm) and JIS B6 next to the ISO B4/B5 (which keep their ISO 216 dimensions for settings saved before them), はがき 100 × 148 mm, 往復はがき 148 × 200 mm, 封筒 長形3号 120 × 235 mm / 長形4号 90 × 225 mm / 角形2号 240 × 332 mm / 角形3号 216 × 277 mm and 四六判 127 × 188 mm. A paper is named by its JSON id or its dialog label, any case and spacing (B5 (JIS) or b5jis), and every added size prints as its own PDF page size. Headline numbers unchanged.

Affinity import (AF.5), brought over from DesignCraft's (storytold/designcraft#291): master pages show on the pages that use them (a locked layer at the bottom); tables open as a text frame per cell and a line per edge; each paragraph keeps its alignment, indents, spacing and leading; frame text takes its text scale, not its frame's; drop shadows and outer glows become live effects, outlines strokes, colour and gradient overlays are baked into the paint; embedded Affinity documents open as editable content, and their artboards no longer become artboards; large pixel layers come in at a reduced resolution; text placed as Affinity places it (lines of differently aligned paragraphs, a frame's first baseline at cap height, last lines whose descenders hang out of the frame), underlines and strikethrough, line breaks inside paragraphs, table cells taller than their row, no stroke on shapes whose stroke style is None, CMYK pixel layers (phone photos in CMYK documents) shown through the document's own CMYK profile instead of the profile-free formula and its blue cast, outlines on stroked shapes. Headline numbers unchanged. Hostile files stay bounded (one budget for the whole read, embedded documents included; overlay work; master page copies), covered by the import fuzzer and limit tests.

About 90 community PRs landed in batches through the full gate, with our fixes on top (formatting, catalog rows, small correctness fixes). New: Objects on Path (#3066), Object › Path › Simplify's slider with Auto-Simplify and More Options (#2555), Pencil Edit Selected Paths redraws the middle of a selected path (#2905), Pencil Tool Options' Alt key toggles to Smooth Tool (#2685), 3D solids built from each stroke's outline (#3049), Live Paint Selection Tool Options (#3052), Locate Selected Objects in the Layers panel (#3033), Snap to Unit for tab stops (#3039), DXF circles and arcs as native entities (#2962), Targa files (#2765), a Georgian interface (#2045), Traditional Chinese status and error messages (#2784), the web page's window.vectorcraft control channel (#2943), select.color (#2939), reproducible export bytes with SOURCEDATEEPOCH (#2947), Spacing Guides on resizes (#2966) and measurement labels on more tools. Fixed: number fields step to the next whole unit (#2916), a click away from edited type makes no new text (#2922), inch rulers in halves (#2951), Recent cards in New Document (#2904), Japanese W-weights in SVG (#2896), the point-type baseline marker (#2897) and the Reshape tool's falloff (#2900). Headline numbers unchanged.

Inch rulers divide the inch in half, not in ten. Zooming in stepped an inch ruler through 0.2, 0.1 and 0.05 of an inch, marks an inch ruler does not carry; below an inch the steps are binary fractions now, 1/2 down to 1/16, with the unlabelled ticks between them binary too (down to 1/128, so the 32nds, 64ths and 128ths appear as the report expects), while the metric units, points, pixels and picas keep their tenths. A label carries the decimals its step needs, so a sixteenth reads 0.0625 rather than the rounded 0.06, with trailing zeros dropped (#2827). Headline numbers unchanged.

Exported and saved files can repeat their bytes: PNG, PDF, EPS, legacy .ai, packaged zips and .vectorcraft saves recorded the wall-clock time they were made in, so the same commands run twice gave different bytes though the pixels matched. SOURCEDATEEPOCH now stands in for the clock in everything a file records, as the reproducible-builds specification defines it; a date a command is given still wins, and a malformed value is ignored rather than refusing the export. The recovery heartbeat and the seed PDF encryption draws on keep the real clock, so a password-protected PDF still differs between runs (#2880). Headline numbers unchanged.

Cursors: 36 more tool states get cursors of their own. Node editing follows the public manual (Direct Selection's anchor squares, Reshape Segment, Group Selection's plus, the arrow hollow on a snap, the Alt-copy arrowheads), the Anchor Point caret, the Curvature pen and Free Transform's side-shear arrows are drawn; Lasso, the freehand, symbolism and other tools borrow a drawn cursor until theirs is drawn. crates/tools/src/cursors.toml lists every cursor for whoever draws them, and cargo xtask cursors warns about one missing from it. Scores unchanged.

Document fonts register every explicitly supplied craft-fonts family after the existing Japanese, Arabic and Thai prefix; optional empty input remains supported. Headline scores and estimates are unchanged.
Brazilian Portuguese (pt-br) covers the whole interface and status/error messages under the completeness tests (#1914); Localization 71% → 74% (measured), hours 55–90 → 50–85.

Direct Selection: deleting an interior anchor of an open path leaves separate surviving runs. Delete/Backspace and history regressions cover the gap; explicit Remove Anchors remains connected. Headline numbers unchanged.

Corner Radius has a link button in Properties and Transform: unlinked, a live rectangle shows a radius field for each corner (#1682). With the Width tool, double-clicking a stroke opens Width Point Edit to create a width point there, and Shift-double-click on a width point opens it with Adjust Adjoining Width Points ticked (#1814, #1630). Holding Alt while dragging a guide out of a ruler switches it between horizontal and vertical (#1782), and a marquee with the Selection or Direct Selection tool also selects the unlocked ruler guides it crosses (#1836). The Transform panel's, Properties panel's and Control bar's X/Y/W/H show and edit only the anchor points selected with Direct Selection (#1839, fixes #1824). With the Direct Selection tool, double-clicking type (including type nested inside a group) switches to the Type tool and puts the caret at the clicked character; pressing Escape finishes editing and returns to the selection tool used before double-clicking, and in isolation mode the first Escape exits editing while preserving isolation until a second Escape. With Snap to Grid on, anchors and objects snap to the grid even when Snap to Pixel is also ticked (#1840; #1816 waits for the reporter). Artboards are deleted the same way from the Artboards panel, its menu, Properties and Delete/Backspace (#1631). The toolbar shows no group labels by default (a preference brings them back) and runs on in one or two columns; the All Tools drawer lists the tools by flyout group with their shortcuts, has a menu (Reset, Basic, Advanced) and a Show section for the Fill/Stroke, Coloring, Draw Mode and Screen Mode controls (#1751). An action clicked in the Actions panel stays selected, so Play Current Selection and Delete Selection act on it (#1853, part of #1629). Redo during a drag keeps the drag as a step (#1856, #1719). Preferences are written as soon as OK is pressed (#1857; #1747 waits for the reporter). Preferences › Appearance of Black › Printing / Exporting and Units › Identify Objects By act (#1750, #1809). The paragraph alignment buttons show none selected for paragraphs with different alignments (#1784); redefining a character style to Auto leading updates the text that uses it and keeps local overrides (#1633); New and Redefine Character Style take the format of the selected text range, also while typing (#1634). Type inside symbols, pattern tiles, graph designs and opacity masks gets its layout bounds back when a native file opens, so warped type in a symbol looks the same after save and reopen (#1833, #1738). Editing, renaming, deleting or merging a global swatch reaches the art of opacity masks (#1830, #1735). macOS: Save As, Save a Copy and the first Save show their sheet again; the sheet's Format menu (#866, reopened) is withdrawn until it can be set before the sheet opens (#1855).

Rendering: copies, symbol instances and repeats that share an appearance keep their stroke outlines between frames (#1667); the canvas no longer reads its whole picture back for each non-isolated group that blends (#1687); envelopes, blends, repeats and meshes redraw when a pattern, symbol, font or colour setting they show changes (#1688); Outline view draws from geometry kept between frames (#1689); CMYK documents with transparency compose their ink planes on several threads (#1755); an edit re-flows a threaded story only when it changes one of the story's frames (#1792); opening a file reads its linked files and lays out its type on the opening thread (#1767). Instances of imported symbols are measured, selected, aligned, culled and exported by their art instead of a 20 pt square (#1744). Export for Screens and the Asset Export panel offer TIFF (#1632). SVG import looks style rules up by id, class and type (#1690), applies :not() selectors (#1799, #1557), no longer stalls on stacked descendant selectors over deep nesting (#1834, #1703) and reads linked files within the automation roots again (#1870). DXF export writes the VPORT view direction once (#1789). Untrusted files: nesting is capped at 32 objects in SVG, PDF, EPS and native files and symbols or patterns that use themselves open without the offending instance or paint (#1852); deeply nested PDF and .ai data, page trees holding themselves and functions or colour spaces built on themselves (#1871), decompression bombs and impossible predictor parameters (#1873, #1700, #1701), brushes that draw themselves (#1872) and hostile EPS, Affinity and native data (#1863: #1715, #1714, #1704, #1699) no longer crash or exhaust the app; the save fallback keeps the old file until the new one is in (#1695). Files whose ids sit at their largest value, a failed command.batch, control requests that timed out and images too large as RGBA for the Eyedropper are handled (#1862: #1718, #1697, #1725, #1717). Effects: wide shadows and glows at high zoom stay within the raster budget, stacked Transform effects are bounded, 3D keeps the area a nonzero compound path fills, pattern tiles redraw when the art they show changes, and a template layer dims its images by Dim Images (#1864: #1706, #1705, #1724, #1723, #1683). A failed save or export is reported in a dialog that names the file and stays until closed (#1865, #1685); a browser download that can't start fails the save (#1693); a file that finishes opening waits while a dialog is open (#1694). krilla's text shaping is no longer built in (#1874, #1730); the CI gate compiles the web app for wasm (#1875).

Image Trace: Shapes finds rounded rectangles and shapes in blurred and scanned art (98 to 100% of the plain-shape inputs, from 57 to 62%; #1845), square-ended lines get square caps (Outline's largest distance 2.94 px to 0.88; #1846), each documented preset has an enhanced version with Auto Grouping and Shapes that measures no worse than the preset (#1847), and blurred or noisy linear gradients trace as one gradient-filled path instead of 3 to 56 (#1848) (docs/image-trace-quality.md). No headline number moves.

Align and Distribute act on the anchor points selected with Direct Selection: the points of one path align to each other, not to the artboard, and Distribute spaces them (#1641, fixes #1636; aligning to a key anchor is still missing). Delete removes every selected anchor of a closed path (it used to remove the wrong ones), removes objects selected whole along with the selected anchors of others, and keeps the remainder selected so a second Delete removes it (#1674). In isolation mode Direct Selection and Group Selection pick only inside the isolated object (#1666). Escape cancels a Direct Selection drag (#1803, #1743). Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802, #1686, #1656). A filled Pencil path keeps a stroke of None (#1804, part of #1679). With the Pen, a press that moves under 3 screen pixels is a click (a corner without handles), and a Precise Cursors command toggles the existing preference and can take a shortcut (#1663). The [ and ] keys reach the Blob Brush, the Eraser and the Symbolism tools in the app (#1734, part of #1661). In the Pathfinder panel a group selected alone counts its nested shapes, so an expanded stroked object keeps the Shape Modes enabled (#1642, #1635). Object › Expand turns radial, grid and mirror repeats into groups of their instances (#1765, #1756). Select › Same matches type on its characters' fill and stroke (#1746, #1737). Fields commit what was typed when you click away or move to another field, as Enter does; Escape still discards it (#1787). Up and Down move through the command search results and Enter runs the highlighted one (#1798, #1757). Slider rails show on Medium Dark (#1808, #1662). On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation). Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed). Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643). Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648). EPS import: a stitched shading keeps its hard colour changes (#1654, #1653). WMF/EMF import refuses an oversized embedded PNG or JPEG from its header, before any pixels are decoded (#1776). PDF open no longer takes exponential time on a crafted name tree with shared nodes when it looks for the editing data (#1781). The size limits on a native file's embedded data also apply to files read from memory, not only streamed ones (#1783). Saving over a private file on Unix no longer leaves a readable temporary copy beside it while the file is written (#1778). An Export for Screens suffix can no longer place files outside the export folder (#1777). Package refuses a folder where it would overwrite the open document or one of its linked files (#1786). ruzstd 0.9.1 fixes a decompression bomb (RUSTSEC-2026-0344) reachable from EPS/.ai and Affinity import (#1807). File Info dates are stamped only after a save succeeds, so a failed save no longer changes them (#1774). Linked files that change during a drag are updated after the drag instead of being missed (#1773). Scatter graph data near the largest number is refused with a message instead of hanging the app (#1780). One very long Liquify stroke segment can no longer create an unbounded number of dabs (#1779). A drag whose last preview failed is no longer recorded as a committed command in the journal that actions and scripts read (#1775). Tests: text import fuzzing no longer searches installed fonts (#1785). Tests: render tests that add fonts no longer race the frame cache tests (#1795). text.create, text.createInPath and the MCP addtext tool take justify, so point type can be centred on or end at its point (#1752, #1748). Control replies are written through a 64 KiB buffer: a 10 MB document.inspect reply over loopback on Windows takes 0.25 s instead of 36 s (#1684). MCP limits: 16 MiB lines, 64-message batches, 256-step commandbatch with 8 MiB of kept results and 256 MiB control replies (#1764, fixes #1727). MCP requires the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and matches control replies by id, and an app refusal without an id reports the app's reason (#1768, fixes #1728). The MCP server reconnects to the app before a call when the connection was closed or holds stray bytes, after an app restart or an idle expiry (#1739). Image Trace, measured in image-trace-quality.md: snap Curves To Lines moves no end of a line by more than 1.6 px, so long lines a degree or two off stay as the image has them (#1647: Technical Drawing's largest distance 4.21 px to 1.46); flat Logo takes the tones a scan's uneven paper makes of one colour for one colour (#1657: on scans 470 paths and 21 px off to 8.5 paths and 0.09 px). No headline number moves.
PngSuite downloads use pinned HTTPS files and a SHA-256 manifest; no archive extraction (#1729).
Synthetic control input has finite click/drag counts and pending-event limits, checked before queue mutation; control-channel bursts yield after 64 requests per frame (#1709).

SVGs that move objects with a CSS transform (translate(100px, 0), rotate(45deg)) or style type with the font shorthand import as drawn (#1565). SVG symbols whose shapes use percentage lengths import at the size and place they are drawn, the percentages being of the symbol's viewBox (#1596). Inkscape's flowed text (flowRoot) opens as area type in its rectangle, a paragraph per flowPara, instead of being dropped, and a region that can't be read is left out with a warning (#1569, fixes #1568). The warning for an unsupported SVG filter names the filter, its primitives and the object, and says the object is drawn without it (#1599, fixes #1598). The pages of an Inkscape multi-page SVG become artboards, named by their labels (#1603, fixes #1601). SVG export with CSS classes or style entities stays fast in documents with many distinct styles (#1567). PDF and .ai import: evenly letter-spaced or tightened type on a path keeps its length along the path instead of closing up to the font's advances (#1586), and type on a path whose stroke is written glyph by glyph comes in as one text object with its stroke, not one object per glyph (#1585). The ICC profiles embedded in JPEG, TIFF and PSD exports have every tag on a 4-byte boundary (ICC.1 §7.1.2), so strict readers accept them (#1589, fixes #1584). GIF, PNG-8 and other indexed exports find each pixel's palette colour through an index instead of a scan, with identical output (#1576). Saving to a network drive on macOS falls back to a plain fsync when the share refuses a full flush (#1625, part of #1620; not confirmed on a real share), and a save still succeeds when a folder refuses the temporary file, the rename over the document or copying permissions: the content is written elsewhere first and copied in, and a failed copy keeps the temporary file and names it (#1649, part of #1620). A document opened by a relative path finds its relatively linked images, and vectorcraft-cli convert lists what reading the input left out as importWarnings (#1606, fixes #1604). A zero-length subpath draws its round cap as a dot and its projecting cap as a square, so dots in imported .ai and SVG files show (#1619, fixes #1613). Pathfinder's Trim, Merge and Crop remove the objects' strokes, and Merge joins same-fill objects whatever their strokes were, as the public Pathfinder page describes (#1572, fixes #1570). Offset Path with an inset larger than the shapes says the offset leaves nothing, instead of asking to select paths (#1591, fixes #1590). The Symbols panel's New Symbol opens Symbol Options to name the symbol first, and Alt-click skips it (#1566, fixes #1560). Tool flyouts are as wide as their longest translated name and shortcut need, so names no longer run into shortcuts in Spanish and other languages (#1650, fixes #1616). Smart Guides: a point drawn with the Pen or a shape tool, and an anchor dragged with Direct Selection, snaps to where paths and ruler guides cross, labelled "intersect" (#1658, part of #1602; a moved selection's own anchors don't). The Transform panel shows a selected ruler guide's X or Y, and typing a value moves it (#1659, part of #1597). This is not established by the documentation we could find: the public help pages on guides, rulers and the Transform, Control and Properties panels (read again on 2026-10-14) describe selecting and dragging unlocked guides and the panels' X and Y for a selection, not a guide's position in a panel, and the one public statement of it is a user's community answer, which is not documentation. It is kept as a convenience pending the owner's decision, with no parity claim and nothing counted towards a score. Select Behind (Ctrl/Cmd-click) tests each object once, so a deep stack of overlapping objects no longer slows it; same objects in the same order (#1571). Commands that take ids run on the objects given with nothing selected, over MCP, the control channel and the CLI too (#1577, fixes #1575). Zig Zag spaces its ridges evenly along each segment, so lines and curves get a regular wave in Corner and Smooth (#1558). Warp › Arc (the effect and Envelope › Make with Warp) bends in the object's real proportions: a circular arc with concentric edges and no fold-over at 100%, so Arc on art that isn't square draws differently from before (#1581, fixes #1578). effect.apply and effect.setParams give an error for a misspelt or wrongly typed effect parameter instead of running the effect with its default (#1623, #1592). Area type in a non-rectangular shape moves a word too wide for the top lines down to the first line that holds it instead of breaking it (#1617, fixes #1615). Stylistic sets (ss01–ss20), stylistic and titling alternates, proportional and lining figures, and superscript and subscript glyphs can be turned on as OpenType features of a character style (text.setStyle {features}), and the OpenType panel keeps them (#1611, fixes #1607). The Polish translator confirmed the Polish rows the maintainers had added after the catalog was written (#1614). No headline number moves.
Control sockets close after bounded idle, partial-line and reply-write waits, returning their connection slot (#1726); existing command processing timeout remains separate.

Image Trace: neighbouring colours share one fitted edge (gaps between them 22 to 50 px of area down to under 2), a 16 megapixel photo traces in 0.9 GB (was 3.9), stroked centre lines lie in the middle of their ink at its width (0.30 to 0.05 px off, 18 to 3 anchors a stroke), nearly level lines are levelled, more sharp corners are kept; new: Ignore Color, the Auto Color and Outline presets, and the Shapes, Auto Grouping and Gradients options (off by default) (docs/image-trace-quality.md).

The interface is available in Polish (pl): menus, panels, dialogs and messages, with one/few/many plurals; AI-drafted, native review pending (#1498). Native documents with a lot of path data (traced or generated art, in layers, symbols or patterns) are saved as compact JSON, about a fifth of the size; small documents stay pretty-printed (#1492). Paste takes a PDF or EPS another app copied as editable vector art: from the macOS pasteboard (with SVG), EPS on Windows beside PDF, and .eps files copied in a file manager, with the new command clipboard.importEps (#1538, fixes #1499). Opening or placing a file with an image too large to decode says so, and the Links panel shows it on the row (#1540, part of #1479). Import: a multi-artboard .ai with notes beside its artboards opens from its editing data, a page's art past its artboard no longer lying over the page before it (#1528); a .ai gradient whose stops are listed upwards keeps each midpoint on the stop that starts its part of the ramp (#1530); SVG text on a path follows basic shapes (circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon) as their SVG 2 equivalent paths (#1531, fixes #1527); PDFs whose alpha soft masks are drawn as images import with the mask instead of empty art (#1551); EPS and PostScript type set in Type 42 (TrueType) fonts imports at its size instead of 1000 times too large (#1553); PDF and EPS import keep a clipping path whose bounding box covers the page but whose shape doesn't (#1544, fixes #1542). Make Compound Path on a group (such as outlined type) keeps the paint of its backmost path instead of drawing nothing, and compound paths joined into one keep their holes (#1537). Live Corners: a round corner next to a curved side curves smoothly instead of sticking out of the shape, and the Smooth tool smooths only the stretch of path under the drag (#1547, fixes #1512). Join merges the selected anchor points that lie on one another, as after Average, into one anchor (#1582, fixes #1533). Guides: Lock Guides also locks the objects made into guides: they can't be selected, moved or deleted (#1543); they are drawn in the guide colour and style of Preferences, and a dragged selection snaps to ruler guides with Smart Guides on (#1583, fixes #1534). Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts lists Edit › Duplicate and the other commands that are in no menu but run without parameters (panel-menu commands such as Break Link to Symbol), so they can be given shortcuts (#1549, #1580, fixes #1539). Raster effects (blur, shadow, glow, grain) drawn after a pattern, radial or freeform gradient fill export at their place and size (#1541, fixes #1536). Fonts: the font scan on Linux also reads the folders fontconfig's configuration lists, such as TeX fonts under /usr/share/texmf/fonts (#1548, fixes #1529; not verified on Linux).

Image Trace's colour presets trace flat art with its own colours however many are asked for (noise no longer shatters it: 16 Colors 70 → 4 paths on the harness's flat art; no slivers of in-between colour along anti-aliased edges), and the photo presets trace a photo into smooth tones without specks or hairlines (High Fidelity Photo 3,653 → 121 paths, colour error 2.30 → 1.75; 16 megapixels traced where 4 were refused) (docs/image-trace-quality.md).

Image Trace traces anti-aliased and blurred images to a fraction of a pixel in Black and White, Grayscale and Color, with corners put back, straight edges as lines and round outlines as circles; a harness measures every preset before and after (docs/image-trace-quality.md): outlines 0.31 → 0.09 px off on average (Default), 0.27 → 0.06 (Black and White Logo).

Effect › 3D and Materials: the light takes the documented Intensity, Rotation, Height, Softness and Ambient Light (to 200 %) and can shine from behind the object, for every 3D type; effects saved with the earlier direction are lit exactly as before.
Effect › 3D and Materials: Perspective is the documented 0°–160° angle for every 3D type, Revolve included; effects saved with the earlier 0–100 % strength look exactly as before.
